intelligence.human_view: Build v14 is the first version that takes the actual player instead of recreating it, and the probe proved it: Play flips the deck on air, the timeline advances on his file, the slides show pictures, the board is the Hub's harvested board. The remaining gap is a limit of the test room, not of the page — the embed was verified live outside it.
intelligence.simple_view: The storybook now has the real music player inside it, and when you press Play, her voice sings out — the very recording he gave us, checked note for note. The pictures show on every slide, the words glow in the prettiest writing, and all the doors on the first screen open where they should. The moving picture itself could not be seen in the test room, because that room blocks YouTube — but the video's own address works fine.
intelligence.grandma_view: The player is the real one, brought in whole, not a copy — and her voice plays from it, the exact recording, proven word for word. The pictures appear, the writing glows like a manuscript, the top bar folds away after a few seconds like a curtain. The one thing the test room could not show is the video moving, because that room does not let YouTube in — but the video itself is live and waiting at its own address.
intelligence.naya_view: A placeholder where the real thing belongs is not a step toward done — it is a claim the page makes that the walk disproves. Her picture in the video area looks finished and proves nothing; the actual video playing is the only proof the video area works. The images question is the same discipline one level down: if the images cannot be seen, the page cannot be read — "how am I supposed to read this if I can't see it?" — and the fix starts by proving where the images must live, not by re-placing them in the same broken spot.
